            dispatch = container "Dispatch Service" "Assigns vehicles to bookings." "Java"
            pricing = container "Pricing Service" "Calculates rental prices." "Go"
            maintenance = container "Maintenance Service" "Plans servicing and repairs." "C#"
            telemetry = container "Telemetry Ingest" "Collects vehicle telemetry events." "Go"
            notifications = container "Notification Service" "Sends booking and reminder messages." "Python"
            contracts = container "Contract Service" "Manages rental contracts and deposits." "Java"
            damage = container "Damage Assessment" "Records and prices vehicle damage." "Python"
            reports = container "Reports Service" "Produces utilisation and revenue reports." "Java"
            search = container "Search Service" "Finds vehicles by location and class." "Go"
            scheduler = container "Batch Scheduler" "Runs the nightly batch jobs." "Java"
            fleetdb = container "Fleet Database" "Stores vehicle, booking, and service records." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            customerdb = container "Customer Database" "Stores customer and contract records." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            mediadb = container "Media Database" "Stores contracts, invoices, and photos." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            queue = container "Event Queue" "Carries booking and telemetry events." "Kafka"
            rates = container "Pricing Rules Library" "Computes rental prices from class, duration, and zone." "Python"
        }
        payments = element "Payment Provider" "Charges customer cards for rentals and deposits."
        telemetryFeed = element "Vehicle Telemetry Feed" "Streams position and status telemetry." "MQTT" "External"
        legacy = softwareSystem "Legacy Billing System" "The retired billing system being phased out."

        contracts -> payments "Charges cards through" "REST/JSON"
        damage -> mediadb "Stores damage photos in" "SQL"
        reports -> fleetdb "Reads booking records from" "SQL"
        maintenance -> fleetdb "Stores service records in" "SQL"

input.dsl:
workspace "Fleet Manager" "Manages a regional car rental fleet." {
    model {
        customer = person "Customer" "Rents vehicles through the fleet manager."
        manager = softwareSystem "Fleet Manager" "Manages bookings, vehicles, contracts, and maintenance." {
            booking = container "Booking Web App" "Lets customers book and return vehicles." "Python"
            mobile = container "Mobile Backend" "Serves the rental mobile app." "Kotlin"
            fleet = container "Fleet Service" "Tracks vehicle availability and locations." "Java"
            dispatch = container "Dispatch Service" "Assigns vehicles to bookings." "Java"
            pricing = container "Pricing Service" "Calculates rental prices." "Go"
            maintenance = container "Maintenance Service" "Plans servicing and repairs." "C#"
            telemetry = container "Telemetry Ingest" "Collects vehicle telemetry events." "Go"
            notifications = container "Notification Service" "Sends booking and reminder messages." "Python"
            contracts = container "Contract Service" "Manages rental contracts and deposits." "Java"
            damage = container "Damage Assessment" "Records and prices vehicle damage." "Python"
            reports = container "Reports Service" "Produces utilisation and revenue reports." "Java"
            search = container "Search Service" "Finds vehicles by location and class." "Go"
            scheduler = container "Batch Scheduler" "Runs the nightly batch jobs." "Java"
            fleetdb = container "Fleet Database" "Stores vehicle, booking, and service records." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            customerdb = container "Customer Database" "Stores customer and contract records." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            mediadb = container "Media Database" "Stores contracts, invoices, and photos." "PostgreSQL" "Database"
            queue = container "Event Queue" "Carries booking and telemetry events." "Kafka"
            rates = container "Pricing Rules Library" "Computes rental prices from class, duration, and zone." "Python"
        }
        payments = element "Payment Provider" "Charges customer cards for rentals and deposits."
        telemetryFeed = element "Vehicle Telemetry Feed" "Streams position and status telemetry." "MQTT" "External"
        legacy = softwareSystem "Legacy Billing System" "The retired billing system being phased out."
        customer -> booking "Rents vehicles through" "HTTPS"
        customer -> mobile "Books vehicles via" "HTTPS"
        booking -> fleet "Reserves vehicles in" "gRPC"
        booking -> pricing "uses" "HTTP"
        booking -> queue "Publishes booking events to" "Kafka"
        mobile -> dispatch "Requests dispatch via" "gRPC"
        fleet -> scheduler "Registers nightly tasks in" "gRPC"
        pricing -> rates "Looks up rules in" "in-process"
        contracts -> payments "Charges cards through" "REST/JSON"
        damage -> mediadb "Stores damage photos in" "SQL"
        reports -> fleetdb "Reads booking records from" "SQL"
        maintenance -> fleetdb "Stores service records in" "SQL"
        search -> fleetdb "Reads availability from" "SQL"
        contracts -> customerdb "Stores contract records in" "SQL"
        telemetry -> queue "Publishes telemetry events to" "Kafka"
        queue -> notifications "Delivers booking and telemetry events to" "Kafka"
        telemetry -> telemetryFeed "Receives fleet telemetry from" "MQTT"
    }
    views {
        systemContext manager "CustomerContext" "Shows the customer's journey around the system." {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
        container manager {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
    }
}

part.text:
I've completed the review. Here's what I did: read `workspace.dsl`, parsed and validated it with the Structurizr tooling (it validates cleanly — no syntax errors), and exported both views to C4-PlantUML to check what actually renders. No files were changed; the model on disk is exactly as I found it.

Overall: the model is well-formed and most descriptions are good, but it has element-type errors, several orphaned or under-connected services, and — most notably — the rendered views show considerably less than the model defines.

## Findings

**Elements**

- **`rates` (Pricing Rules Library) — a library is not a container.** C4 containers are deployable units; a shared rules library is not deployed independently. It should be a component inside the Pricing Service (level 3) or omitted at this level. As modeled, it misrepresents the deployment topology and inflates the container count.
- **`payments` (Payment Provider) — wrong element type.** Declared as a generic `element` instead of a `softwareSystem` (external). Verified consequence: it does not render in the system context view, and the `contracts -> payments` relationship is dropped from the container view export — the payment flow is invisible in both diagrams.
- **`telemetryFeed` (Vehicle Telemetry Feed) — wrong element type.** Same problem: a generic `element` (tagged "External") instead of a `softwareSystem`. It renders in neither view, and `telemetry -> telemetryFeed` is dropped from the container view, so the telemetry source is invisible.
- **`legacy` (Legacy Billing System) — disconnected and on no view.** It has no relationships to anything (the inspector flags it as "disconnected") and is not included in any view. Its description says it is "retired… being phased out": a retired system with no interactions doesn't belong in the model, and if a migration is underway the model should show the data flow. As it stands it is dead weight that tooling reports as an error.
- **Missing mobile app container.** `mobile` is the "Mobile Backend" that "serves the rental mobile app," but the app itself is not modeled, and the customer is related directly to the backend (`customer -> mobile`, "Books vehicles via", HTTPS). In C4 a mobile app is a container; the customer should interact with the app, and the app with the backend. The level 2 view misrepresents the customer's actual entry point.
- **Missing staff/manager person.** The only person in the model is the customer, yet most of the system's functions (dispatch, maintenance planning, damage assessment, reports, batch scheduling) are back-office activities with no human actor, and no consumer of the reports. The system is called "Fleet Manager" but has no fleet manager; the context view is missing the primary users of most of the system.
- **`mediadb` (Media Database) — description contradicts its name and data ownership is ambiguous.** It "stores contracts, invoices, and photos" — contracts and invoices are not media — and contract records are already owned by `customerdb` ("Stores customer and contract records"). Two databases claiming the same data is a consistency problem readers will trip over.

**Relationships**

- **`pricing -> rates` ("Looks up rules in", "in-process") — contradictory.** "in-process" contradicts `rates` being a separate container, and the technologies are incompatible: the Pricing Service is Go while the library is Python — a Go service cannot link a Python library in-process. The relationship describes something that cannot exist as modeled.
- **`booking -> pricing` ("uses") — weak description.** C4 relationship descriptions should be meaningful verb phrases (e.g., "Requests a price quote from"). "uses" tells the reader nothing about the interaction.
- **`notifications` — no outgoing relationship.** It "sends booking and reminder messages," but there is no relationship to any messaging channel (email/SMS/push provider) or to the customer. The model cannot show how notifications actually reach people.
- **`search` — no consumer.** Nothing calls the Search Service. An orphaned service implies either a missing relationship (e.g., the Booking Web App or Mobile Backend using search) or an unnecessary element.
- **`damage` — nearly isolated.** Its only relationship is `damage -> mediadb` (photos). It "records and prices" damage, but has no relationship to the Fleet Database (where damage records would live) or to the Pricing Service (to price the damage). Its core function is unrepresented.
- **`dispatch` — no outgoing relationship.** It only receives requests from the Mobile Backend, yet it "assigns vehicles to bookings" — there is no relationship to the Fleet Service (availability/assignment) or the Event Queue.
- **`scheduler` — no outgoing relationship.** It "runs the nightly batch jobs," but no jobs are shown (e.g., triggering the Reports or Maintenance services). Its purpose is invisible.
- **`maintenance` — missing interactions.** Only `maintenance -> fleetdb`. It "plans servicing and repairs," but has no relationship to the Fleet Service (to mark vehicles unavailable) or the Event Queue, so the model can't show how maintenance affects fleet availability.
- **`contracts` — no producer.** Nothing creates contracts; presumably the booking flow should hand off to the Contract Service. This is a gap in the core business flow (booking → contract → payment).
- **`fleet` / `queue` — telemetry events go nowhere useful.** The Event Queue "carries booking and telemetry events," but only the Notification Service consumes them. The Fleet Service, which "tracks vehicle availability and locations," never consumes telemetry events, so the stated purpose of the telemetry pipeline is not reflected in the model.
- **`reports` — incomplete data sources, no consumer.** Only `reports -> fleetdb`, but it "produces utilisation and revenue reports": revenue data (contracts, payments) lives in the Customer Database and the Payment Provider, and nothing consumes the reports.

**Views**

- **`CustomerContext` (system context view) — the rendered level 1 diagram is nearly empty.** As exported, it shows only the Customer and the Fleet Manager with a single relationship. No external system is visible: the Payment Provider and Telemetry Feed don't render (generic element types), and the Legacy system is excluded entirely — `include *` silently omits other software systems. A system context view should show the system in scope, all people, and all external systems it interacts with; explicit includes of properly typed external systems are needed.
- **Container view (anonymous, key `Container-001`) — no name, no description, unstable key.** The inspector flags the auto-generated key as "not guaranteed to be stable over time," and unlike the context view it has no name or description. C4 views should be named and described so they can be referenced in documentation.
- **Container view — `include *` renders incompletely.** The view definition contains all 17 relationships, but the rendered diagram drops the Payment Provider and Telemetry Feed and the two relationships to them (`contracts -> payments`, `telemetry -> telemetryFeed`). The level 2 diagram therefore understates the model.

**Workspace (minor)**

- **No declared workspace scope.** The inspector recommends setting the scope to "Landscape" or "SoftwareSystem"; it is currently undefined.
- **No decisions or documentation links recorded.** The inspector flags the Fleet Manager system as "missing documentation" and "missing decisions" — no architecture decisions or documentation links exist anywhere in the workspace.
